research_question: Is live previous-target pose, rather than bounded clipping/action-chart conversion alone, causally required for zero-training PPO transfer from achieved-relative pd_ee_delta_pose to target-relative pd_ee_target_delta_pose?

arms.source: source policy and original achieved-relative native controller
arms.naive: frozen policy 7-D direct-copy action to target controller with source observation restored
arms.strict: source intended physical target reconstructed from achieved EE, invert actual previous target pose; refuse nonrepresentable controls
arms.memory_projected: same inversion but explicitly mark nonexact clipped/projected translation box and rotation unit ball
arms.memory_blind_projected: identical source intended physical target and identical normalization/bounded projection, but *intentionally substitute current achieved target-arm EE pose for the true previous target pose* when calculating the target-relative command

primary_endpoint: official simulator info.success ever true by 50 steps for each arm; one row per seed and all five arms
primary_paired_contrast: memory_projected minus memory_blind_projected, paired per original physical reset seed
secondary_endpoints: stateblind projection steps vs memoryaware projection steps
projected-only and stateless-only discordant pair counts
record all initialization, refusal and projection amplitudes
prohibited: tuning projection scaling on these holdout seeds
using previous known seeds as new test
using test outcomes to select a winner
interpretation: A strong paired advantage would isolate *use of live controller target memory* under the same rotation, scaling, clipping and source policy, not prove novel first-ever adapter, formal safety, or real-world transfer. A null/negative result rejects this mechanism claim for this task.
